title: personal-index-requests v1
description: Envelope published by Modules 09-12 onto `personal-index-requests` after their global indexing step succeeds, and consumed by Module 25 to build the per-user ArcadeDB index. Enforced at publish time: an invalid event is rejected by the publisher, not by the consumer, so a malformed payload never reaches the topic. Entry payloads are deliberately open (`additionalProperties: true`) — Module 25 maps the fields it knows and ignores the rest, so a worker can add a field without a coordinated schema bump.

event_id.description: sha256(asset_path + version_id + user_id), lowercase hex. The consumer's deduplication key: replays of the same asset version for the same user are acknowledged and dropped rather than reindexed.

schema_version.description: Pinned by V04-2. Present so a future v2 consumer can route by version instead of guessing.

source_module.description: Which worker published this. Diagnostic only — the consumer routes on entry `type`, not on this.

branch_id.description: The owning user (JWT `sub`). Routes to database `user_{branch_id}`. Without it the consumer cannot place the data and skips the entry.

version_id.description: Asset version. Used for delete-by-version and as part of event_id.

asset_path.description: Object-storage path of the source asset. Part of event_id.

chunks.description: Document/audio chunks. Each entry needs `type` and content (`text` or `summary`); `embedding` is optional — the consumer embeds with BGE-M3 when absent.

moments.description: Video moments. Merged with `chunks` by the consumer.

id.description: Chunk id. Also the Redis per-chunk dedup key, which is a finer layer than event_id: event_id stops a whole replayed message, `id` stops a single chunk that arrives twice across different messages.

payload.description: Entry fields. May be nested here or flat on the entry itself — the consumer accepts both.
